alternatives.reason: Constitution: consumer fixtures are never mutated. The consumer's docs/ai/context-pack.json stays a read-only observation (declared context); the rebuilt pack lives in governance state and is the live context.
UI-20 acceptance: the AI must not turn a gap into a fact. A missing source is listed with the stages it blocks, carries no content hash, and the pack is PARTIAL until the file exists.
Would mutate the fixture. Instead the operator declares an additional required document in a new baseline version; the declaration is verified against the repository, never created.

The pack records the topology version and config hash for lineage, but drift is measured on document sources and the baseline version only; topology drift already invalidates decisions through VS-003.

architecture_impact: Adds internal/document: a versioned document baseline per Project (v1 bootstrapped from project.yaml document declarations with their requiredFor stages; DECLARE / WITHDRAW create new versions guarded by expected_version, audited). Manifest declarations cannot be withdrawn here.

Every declared document is observed read-only under the consumer root (stat + sha256); derived documents keep the registry verdict (DERIVED / STALE with stale sources). Document readiness per stage (decision, development, work-order, staging) is NEEDS_INPUT when a required document is MISSING.

Context Pack rebuild (CP-nnn, context-pack/v1 shape extended): sources with path / version / content hash / status, missing list with readiness impact, readiness by stage, decision refs (repository DRs + ledger DECs), limitations, baseline and topology lineage, source_snapshot_hash and pack_hash. PARTIAL while any declared source is missing; nothing is synthesized. Live context = latest pack status, STALE when sources or the baseline moved after generation.

Change ledger integration: change.RegistrySource overlays the baseline (live document set, live context status, document readiness for decisions). A missing decision document makes a new Change NEEDS_INPUT with owner project_owner; the decision snapshot hash binds the declared set, so declaring a new required document after a decision marks it STALE by design.
HTTP: GET/POST /documents, POST /documents/withdraw, POST /context-pack/rebuild, GET /context-pack/{pack}; /healthz reports documents: baseline-versioned.

Frontend: Documents / AI Context panel replaces the read-only list — readiness per stage, declared documents with version / hash / status, declare form, withdraw with reason, rebuild form, pack card with missing list, sources, readiness, decision refs, limitations, audit.
cost_assumptions: No cloud resources; JSON state only.
unknowns: Declaring a required document is the only way to demonstrate a gap without mutating fixtures; a real consumer repository would show gaps by simply lacking files the manifest declares.
Firestore persistence and actor verification remain the caveats of DR-005…DR-009.
acceptance_criteria: UI-20: declaring a missing document marks decision and staging NEEDS_INPUT naming the file, development stays READY; the rebuilt pack is PARTIAL, lists the missing source with the stages it blocks, shows path / version / content hash for present sources and the audit trail; a new Change reports decision_documents as a missing input naming the file; withdrawing restores READY and a rebuild is DERIVED; the consumer tree is byte-identical.
The consumer's own docs/ai/context-pack.json status (e.g. STALE with stale sources) stays visible as declared context.
